mainTopic: ה׳'s justice and kindness, the י״ג מדות, and the power of תשובה to tear up a גזר דין
overview: The amud opens with the end of an earlier דרשה: ה׳ forgives the humble person who sees himself as a 'leftover'. Three אמוראים then point out פסוקים that call ה׳ both strictly just and kind. Each answers the same way: בתחלה ה׳ judges with strict justice, and לבסוף He acts with חסד. Next, רבי יוחנן explains that ה׳ showed משה the י״ג מדות as a set prayer for forgiveness, and רב יהודה adds that a ברית promises these מדות are never unanswered. רבי יוחנן then teaches that תשובה can tear up a גזר דין that has already been issued, and אביי proves this from the word ״ורפא לו״. The גמרא tests this teaching against a ברייתא about repenting before יום כיפור, a ברייתא about rain, and the sailors in תהלים 107. These tests lead to the rule that a צבור's תשובה can tear up a decree, while a יחיד's cannot after the decree is sealed. Finally, בלוריא הגיורת asks about two clashing פסוקים on ה׳ showing favor. רבי יוסי הכהן answers with a parable, and the amud ends just as רבי עקיבא's different answer is introduced on the next amud.

steps.title: Forgiveness is for the one who sees himself as a 'leftover'
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier דרשה‎: ה׳ forgives sins for the person who makes himself like 'leftovers', meaning humble.
steps.simpleTranslation: …for the one who makes himself like leftovers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a teaching that started before this section. ה׳ forgives the sins of a person who sees himself as small and unimportant, like a leftover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier דרשה explained the words 'לשארית נחלתו' ('to the remnant of His inheritance'). The word שארית (remnant) is read as שיריים (leftovers). So forgiveness goes to the humble person who doesn't put himself first.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftovers, what remains after the main part is gone

steps.whatToRemember: Humility, seeing yourself as a 'leftover', is what brings ה׳'s forgiveness.

phrases.english: For one who makes himself like leftovers.
phrases.notes: This finishes a דרשה on 'לשארית נחלתו' (מיכה 7:18). The word שארית, remnant, is being read as 'leftovers'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a דרשה that began earlier on the daf
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ה׳'s forgiveness is given to the humble person who sees himself as secondary.

steps.title: רב הונא: Is ה׳ righteous or kind?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא points out that one פסוק calls ה׳ both צדיק (strictly just) and חסיד (kind beyond the letter of the law).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא pointed out a contradiction. It is written, 'ה׳ is righteous in all His ways,' and it is written, 'and kind in all His works'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא notices that one פסוק seems to describe ה׳ in two opposite ways. It calls Him strictly fair, and it also calls Him generous beyond what is fair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צדיק gives exactly what is deserved. A חסיד gives more than what is deserved. The question is how the same פסוק can describe ה׳'s ways with both words.

keyTerms.meaning: Points out a contradiction (literally, 'throws' two sources against each other)
It is written … and it is written: the formula for setting two texts against each other
Kind, going beyond what the law requires

phrases.english: Rav Huna raised a contradiction:
It is written: 'ה׳ is righteous in all His ways,'
and it is written: 'and kind in all His works'!
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the very same פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a series of contradictions about דין and חסד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Strict justice (צדיק) and going beyond justice (חסיד) seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: At first righteous, in the end kind
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the two describe different stages: first ה׳ is צדיק, and afterward He is חסיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, He is righteous, and in the end, He is kind.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers his own question. Both words are true, but at different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both descriptions are true; they belong to different stages. One common explanation: when ה׳ judges, He is strictly fair, and when it comes time to carry out the punishment, He is kind and softens it.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying ה׳ stops being just. Both are true. They just apply at different stages.

phrases.english: At first: righteous,
and in the end: kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 2
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to say ה׳ is both strict and kind at the same time
steps.terutzMaskana: Strictness comes first, and kindness comes afterward

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: Kindness or exact payback?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר points out a פסוק that says kindness belongs to ה׳, yet also says He pays each person according to his deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר pointed out a contradiction. It is written, 'And to You, ה׳, belongs kindness,' and it is written, 'for You repay a man according to his deeds.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא raises the same kind of question from a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חסד means giving more than deserved. 'According to his deeds' means giving exactly what is deserved. Both appear in the same פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Kindness, giving beyond what is earned

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar raised a contradiction:
It is written: 'And to You, ה׳, belongs kindness,'
and it is written: 'for You repay a man according to his deeds.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel contradiction from a different פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Kindness beyond what is deserved clashes with exact measure-for-measure repayment.

steps.title: At first exact payback, in the end kindness
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that first ה׳ repays according to deeds, and in the end He acts with חסד.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, 'for You repay according to his deeds'; and in the end, 'and to You, ה׳, belongs kindness.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the same kind of answer as רב הונא. Exact justice comes first, and kindness comes later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice the order. The פסוק mentions kindness first, but רבי אלעזר says it actually comes last. The order of the words is not the order in which things happen.

phrases.english: At first: 'for You repay according to his deeds,'
and in the end: 'and to You, ה׳, belongs kindness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 4 using רב הונא's pattern
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Kindness and exact payback seem to happen at the same time
steps.terutzMaskana: Exact payback comes first, and kindness comes afterward

steps.title: אילפי: Abundant kindness or truth?
steps.stepSummary: אילפי (or אילפא) points out that one of the י״ג מדות describes ה׳ as both 'abundant in kindness' and 'truth'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אילפי, and some say אילפא, pointed out a contradiction. It is written, 'and abundant in kindness,' and it is written, 'and truth.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא raises the same kind of question, this time from the list of ה׳'s attributes in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמת (truth) points to strict justice, where everything is exactly as deserved. רב חסד points to great kindness beyond justice.

phrases.english: Ilfai, and some say Ilfa, raised a contradiction:
It is written: 'and abundant in kindness,'
and it is written: 'and truth.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילְפַי, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אִילְפָא רָמֵי, כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third parallel contradiction, from the י״ג מדות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Great kindness seems to clash with strict truth and justice.

steps.title: At first truth, in the end abundant kindness
steps.stepSummary: אילפי answers that first ה׳ acts with אמת (strict justice), and in the end with abundant חסד.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, 'and truth'; and in the end, 'and abundant in kindness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The third contradiction gets the same answer. Strict truth comes first, and great kindness comes afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the order is flipped from the order of the words in the פסוק. All three אמוראים agree on one idea. ה׳ begins with strict justice and finishes with kindness.
steps.whatToRemember: All three contradictions have the same answer. בתחלה, at first, ה׳ judges with strict justice. לבסוף, in the end, He acts with חסד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This fits the theme of ראש השנה: the judgment is real and exact, but ה׳'s kindness has the final word.

phrases.english: At first: 'and truth,'
and in the end: 'and abundant in kindness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 6 with the same pattern
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Truth and abundant kindness seem to apply together
steps.terutzMaskana: Strict truth comes first, and abundant kindness comes afterward

steps.title: ה׳ shows משה the order of prayer like a prayer leader
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads ״ויעבור ה׳ על פניו ויקרא״ as ה׳ wrapping Himself like a שליח צבור and teaching משה a set order of prayer that brings forgiveness.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "And ה׳ passed before him and called out." רבי יוחנן said: If a פסוק did not say this, we could never say it. It teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא wrapped Himself like a שליח צבור and showed משה the order of prayer. He told him: Whenever Israel sins, let them do this order before Me, and I will forgive them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the פסוק that introduces the י״ג מדות, and רבי יוחנן explains what it shows. ה׳, as it were, teaches משה how to pray for forgiveness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״ויעבור... ויקרא״ are read as ה׳ acting like a prayer leader who stands up and calls out the prayer. The lesson is practical: Israel is given a set prayer, saying the מדות, that brings מחילה. רבי יוחנן admits the image is so bold that only a פסוק allows us to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: Were it not written in a פסוק. A signal that the idea is very bold.
Wrapped Himself, as in a טלית
The prayer leader who leads the community

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying ה׳ has a body or wears clothing. His phrase ״אי אפשר לאומרו״ shows he knows this is a picture we may only use because the פסוק itself suggests it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for reciting the י״ג מדות in סליחות as a request for forgiveness.

phrases.english: "And ה׳ passed by before him, and called out."
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Were it not written in a verse,
it would be impossible to say it.
phrases.notes: The idea is so bold that we could not say it on our own. We may only say it because the פסוק hints at it.

phrases.english: It teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, wrapped Himself
like a prayer leader,
and showed Moshe the order of prayer.
He said to him:
Whenever Israel sins,
let them do before Me according to this order,
and I will forgive them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אִלְמָלֵא מִקְרָא כָּתוּב, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאוֹמְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 6 quoted one of the י״ג מדות. Now the גמרא goes back to the opening of that passage and explains its purpose as a prayer for forgiveness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ taught משה that reciting the י״ג מדות in this set order brings forgiveness whenever Israel sins.

steps.title: Why ה׳'s name is said twice
steps.stepSummary: The double ״ה׳ ה׳״ means ה׳ is the same merciful God before a person sins and after he sins and does תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "ה׳‎, ה׳" means: I am He before a person sins, and I am He after a person sins and does תשובה. So He is "a merciful and gracious God."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first words of the י״ג מדות, where ה׳'s name appears twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each mention of the name stands for a different time: one before the sin and one after the sin and the תשובה. The message is that sinning and doing תשובה does not change how ה׳ relates to the person. He is still ״אל רחום וחנון״.

phrases.english: I am He before a person sins,
and I am He after a person sins
and does repentance:
"a merciful and gracious God."

steps.triggerLanguage: ״ה׳ ה׳״ — אֲנִי הוּא קוֹדֶם שֶׁיֶּחְטָא הָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After introducing the י״ג מדות as a prayer, the גמרא begins explaining the actual words, starting with ״ה׳ ה׳״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The repeated name teaches that ה׳ stays the same merciful God both before a sin and after the sinner does תשובה.

steps.title: A covenant that the thirteen מדות are always answered
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה teaches that a ברית was made that the י״ג מדות never come back empty, based on ״הנה אנכי כורת ברית״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: A covenant was made for the thirteen מדות that they do not return empty, as it says: "Behold, I make a covenant."
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה adds a promise. Praying with the י״ג מדות is guaranteed to have an effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after the passage of the מדות, the תורה says ״הנה אנכי כורת ברית״. רב יהודה reads this as a covenant tied to those מדות themselves. It strengthens the promise from step 8: these prayers ״אינן חוזרות ריקם״, they never come back without an answer.
steps.whatToRemember: ה׳ taught the י״ג מדות as a prayer, the double ״ה׳״ shows His mercy before and after a sin, and a ברית promises these מדות are never unanswered.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
A covenant was made for the thirteen attributes
that they do not return empty,
as it says: "Behold, I make a covenant."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: בְּרִית כְּרוּתָה לִשְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה מִדּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It adds a guarantee to the prayer described in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The י״ג מדות are backed by a covenant and never go unanswered.

steps.title: תשובה can tear up a decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that תשובה is so great it tears up a person's גזר דין, based on ״ושב ורפא לו״ in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Great is תשובה, because it tears up a person's decree, as it says: "Make the heart of this people fat, make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes, lest they see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and return and be healed."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching from רבי יוחנן about how powerful תשובה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes a people under a harsh decree. Still, it says that if they did return, they would be healed. This shows that even after a decree is issued, תשובה can cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: A sentence or decree that has already been issued
And he will return and be healed

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a judgment already decreed is not final, because תשובה can still change it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Great is repentance,
for it tears up a person's sentence,
as it says: "Make the heart of this people fat,
make their ears heavy, and smear over their eyes,
lest they see with their eyes,
and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart,
and return, and be healed."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמְּקָרַעַת גְּזַר דִּינוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching that follows the theme of forgiveness from the previous steps, now focused on the power of תשובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תשובה can cancel a decree that has already been issued against a person.

steps.title: Maybe תשובה only helps before the sentence is decreed
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי whether רבי יוחנן's teaching might apply only before the גזר דין is issued.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But maybe the פסוק is talking about תשובה before the sentence is decreed?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's proof. He suggests the פסוק may only mean that תשובה helps before a decree is made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said תשובה tears up a decree that was already issued. רב פפא offers a weaker reading: maybe תשובה only stops a decree from being made in the first place. If so, the פסוק would not prove that a finished decree can be torn up.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But perhaps it means before the sentence is decreed?
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק from ישעיהו that רבי יוחנן quoted might only be about stopping a decree before it is made.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far רבי יוחנן's proof from ״ושב ורפא לו״ really reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that תשובה tears up a decree already issued.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק could be read as speaking only about the time before a decree, so it does not prove that a finished decree can be undone.

steps.title: Healing means there is already a sickness
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the word ״ורפא לו״ (healing) shows the sentence was already in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is written ״and be healed.״ What kind of thing needs healing? You must say: a sentence that was already decreed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי יוחנן. He points to the word ״רפא״ (heal) in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only heal something that is already sick. So the פסוק must be talking about a person whose decree is already in place, and תשובה still heals it. This rejects רב פפא's weaker reading.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say (only one option is left)

phrases.english: He said to him:
"And be healed" is written,
Which thing needs healing?
You must say: this is a sentence already decreed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Close reading of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe תשובה only helps before a decree is issued.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word ״רפא״ shows the decree already exists, and תשובה still heals it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This fixes the strong version of רבי יוחנן's teaching: תשובה can undo even a finished decree. The next challenges all attack this version.

steps.title: A ברייתא says only repentance before יום כיפור helps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן with a ברייתא: if someone did not repent between ראש השנה and יום כיפור, nothing will help him afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: One who repents in between is forgiven. One who did not repent in between, even if he brought all the finest rams in the world, is not forgiven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says there is a window between ראש השנה and יום כיפור. After that window closes and the decree is sealed, even the best קרבנות will not bring forgiveness. That seems to say a finished decree cannot be torn up, which goes against רבי יוחנן and אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: In between (here, between ראש השנה and יום כיפור)
Rams of Nebaioth, famous for their fine quality

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who repents in between is forgiven;
phrases.notes: "In between" means the days between ראש השנה and יום כיפור.

phrases.english: if he did not repent in between,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הֵבִיא כׇּל אֵילֵי נְבָיוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם
phrases.english: even if he brought all the rams of Nebaioth in the world
he is not forgiven!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of Step 13 that תשובה works even after the decree.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's teaching, as defended by אביי, that תשובה tears up a decree already issued.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits forgiveness to the time before יום כיפור. After that, nothing helps, so a sealed decree seems unchangeable.

steps.title: An individual is different from a community
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a יחיד, while רבי יוחנן's teaching is about a צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one is about an individual, and that one is about a community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each source is talking about a different kind of person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a יחיד, תשובה only helps before the decree is sealed on יום כיפור. When a צבור repents, the power is greater, and it can tear up even a sealed decree. So רבי יוחנן's teaching stands, but only for a community.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (the contradiction can be settled)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about an individual,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the ברייתא, where repenting after יום כיפור does not help.

phrases.english: that one is about a community.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — בְּיָחִיד, הָא — בְּצִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say no one can change a sealed decree.
steps.terutzMaskana: A sealed decree cannot be changed for a יחיד, but a צבור's תשובה can tear it up.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule so far: a יחיד must repent before יום כיפור. When a צבור repents, it can tear up even a sealed גזר דין.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think תשובה of a יחיד after יום כיפור is worthless. The גמרא here is only discussing whether it cancels the decree that was already sealed for that year.

steps.title: A ברייתא on rain: even a repentant nation cannot get more rain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: if כלל ישראל was wicked on ראש השנה and then repented, the small amount of rain decreed cannot be increased. ה׳ only makes it fall at the right time and place.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: "The eyes of ה׳ your God are upon it" means sometimes for good and sometimes for bad. Sometimes for good, how? If Israel was completely wicked on ראש השנה and little rain was decreed for them, and in the end they repented, it is impossible to add rain, because the decree was already issued. Instead ה׳ brings the rain at the right times, on land that needs it, all according to the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against Step 15. It brings a ברייתא showing that even when the whole nation repents, a decree already issued stays as it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the whole community of ישראל repented, which should be the case of a צבור. Yet the ברייתא says the amount of rain cannot be added to, because the decree is already set. ה׳ can only use the small amount wisely, so this seems to contradict the idea that a צבור's תשובה tears up the decree.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"The eyes of the Lord your God are upon it":
sometimes for good, sometimes for bad.
Sometimes for good: how so?

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל רְשָׁעִים גְּמוּרִין בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
phrases.english: Suppose Israel were completely wicked on Rosh Hashanah
and a small amount of rain was decreed for them,
and in the end they repented.
To add to the rain is impossible,
since the decree was already issued.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מוֹרִידָן בִּזְמַנָּן,
phrases.english: Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings it down at its proper time,
on the land that needs it,
all according to the needs of the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: ״עֵינֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ בָּהּ״ — עִתִּים לְטוֹבָה עִתִּים לְרָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new objection against the answer of Step 15 (that a צבור's תשובה tears up the decree).
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a צבור's תשובה can tear up a sealed decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All of ישראל repented, which is a צבור, yet the rain decree could not be increased. This suggests even a צבור cannot undo the decree itself.

steps.title: The other side: a righteous nation that sinned cannot get less rain
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if ישראל was righteous on ראש השנה and much rain was decreed, and then they sinned, the rain cannot be reduced. ה׳ makes it fall at the wrong times and in places that do not need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes for bad, how? If Israel was completely righteous on ראש השנה and much rain was decreed for them, and in the end they turned away, it is impossible to reduce it, because the decree was already issued. Instead ה׳ brings the rain at the wrong times, on land that does not need it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with the opposite case, where a righteous nation sinned. The next step shows which part of the ברייתא the גמרא actually uses for its challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirror case shows the same pattern from the other side: once the amount of rain is decreed, it stays the same. Only the timing and place of the rain change. The גמרא's challenge, though, rests on the good case, where the nation repented. That is why Step 18 opens with 'לטובה מיהא', 'for the good, at least'.

phrases.english: Sometimes for bad: how so?

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִין בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
phrases.english: Suppose Israel were completely righteous on Rosh Hashanah
and a large amount of rain was decreed for them,
and in the end they turned away.
To reduce the rain is impossible,
since the decree was already issued.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מוֹרִידָן שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַנָּן,
phrases.english: Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings it down not at its proper time,
on land that does not need it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 16 with the mirror case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from Step 15 that a צבור's תשובה tears up a sealed decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This half of the ברייתא is quoted to complete the source. The attack itself comes from the good case (Step 16), as Step 18 makes explicit with 'לטובה מיהא'.
steps.confusionAlert: Both cases use ״חזרו בהן״, but they mean opposite things. In the good case they returned to ה׳, and in the bad case they turned away from Him.

steps.title: Why not tear up the sentence and add rain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presses the ברייתא from Step 16. When ישראל repented, why does ה׳ not tear up the decree and give more rain? This suggests even a צבור's decree cannot be torn up.
steps.simpleTranslation: At least in the good case, where they repented, let ה׳ tear up their sentence and add more rain for them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the challenge from the rain ברייתא against רבי יוחנן. In the case where ישראל repented, ה׳ should simply cancel the decree and give extra rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said a small amount of rain was decreed, ישראל repented, and the amount still was not increased. If רבי יוחנן is right that a צבור's תשובה tears up the decree, ה׳ should add rain. Since He does not, it looks like even a צבור cannot change the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: let Him tear it up (cancel it)

phrases.english: For the good, at least,
phrases.notes: This is the case from Step 16, where ישראל was wicked on ראש השנה but then repented.

phrases.english: let Him tear up their sentence
and add for them!
phrases.notes: Add more rain than the small amount first decreed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the sharp inference from the ברייתא of Steps 16-17 against רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's teaching that a צבור's תשובה tears up the גזר דין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a צבור's תשובה could tear up the decree, ה׳ would add rain after they repented. The ברייתא says He does not, so the decree must stay in place.

steps.title: There, a different solution was possible
steps.stepSummary: The rain case is different. ה׳ can help the community just as well by sending the rain at the right time and place, so there is no need to tear up the decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it is possible to help them in this other way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. In the rain case ה׳ had another way to help, so He did not need to tear up the decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not prove that a צבור's decree cannot be torn up. It only shows that when the same good result can come through timing, with the rain falling when and where it is needed, ה׳ uses that path. רבי יוחנן's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: it is possible in this way

phrases.english: It is different there,
because it is possible in this way.
phrases.notes: "This way" means making the small amount of rain fall at the right time and in the right place, as in Step 16.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the rain case had another solution available.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא proves a צבור's decree can never be torn up.
steps.terutzMaskana: ה׳ does not tear up the decree only because the community can be helped through the timing and place of the rain. רבי יוחנן's rule still stands.

steps.title: The sailors in תהלים 107
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new challenge by quoting the פסוקים about sailors in a storm who cry out to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "Those who go down to the sea in ships, who do work in great waters, they saw the works of ה׳... He spoke and raised a stormy wind that lifted up its waves. They reel and stagger like a drunk... Then they cried out to ה׳ in their trouble... Let them thank ה׳ for His kindness..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new challenge by quoting a set of פסוקים about sailors. This step sets up the point that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These פסוקים describe sailors caught in a storm who cry out to ה׳. The quote is only the setup. The challenge itself comes from the special markers on these verses, explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: those who go down to the sea (sailors)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"Those who go down to the sea in ships,
who do work in great waters.
They saw the works of ה׳, etc.
He spoke and raised a stormy wind
which lifted up its waves.
They reel and stagger like a drunk, etc.

phrases.aramaic: וַיִּצְעֲקוּ אֶל ה׳ בַּצַּר לָהֶם וְגוֹ׳
phrases.english: Then they cried out to ה׳ in their trouble, etc.
Let them thank ה׳ for His kindness, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rain challenge is answered, the גמרא brings a new source against רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's teaching that a צבור's תשובה tears up the decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The attack comes in Step 21.

steps.title: Crying out after the decree is not answered
steps.stepSummary: Markers are placed on these פסוקים, like the limiting words of the תורה. They teach that crying out before the גזר דין is answered, but crying out after it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He made markers for them, like the words "אך" and "רק" in the תורה, to tell you: if they cried out before the sentence, they are answered; if they cried out after the sentence, they are not answered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the point of the sailor פסוקים and turns it into a challenge. The markers teach that crying out after the גזר דין does not help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Words like "אך" and "רק" in the תורה limit a rule. In the same way, these markers limit the promise that ה׳ answers people who cry out to Him. A group of sailors sounds like many people, so it seems that even a group's prayer cannot change a decree, against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: markers or signs placed in the text
the words "אך" and "רק" ("but" and "only"), which limit a rule

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the markers as saying these people are never answered. Crying out before the גזר דין works. Only crying out after it does not.

phrases.english: He made markers for them
phrases.notes: In a ספר תהלים you can see a special upside-down letter נ placed next to these verses.

phrases.english: like the "but"s and "only"s in the תורה,
phrases.notes: Words like אך and רק narrow a rule, so here the markers narrow when crying out works.

phrases.english: to tell you:
if they cried out before the sentence, they are answered;

phrases.aramaic: צָעֲקוּ לְאַחַר גְּזַר דִּין — אֵינָן נַעֲנִין!
phrases.english: if they cried out after the sentence, they are not answered!

steps.triggerLanguage: עָשָׂה לָהֶן סִימָנִיּוֹת כְּאַכִּין וְרַקִּין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the sailor פסוקים from Step 20 and draws the challenge from them.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's teaching that a צבור's תשובה tears up the decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A whole group of sailors cries out after the decree and is not answered. This suggests that a group's prayer cannot tear up a גזר דין either.

steps.title: Sailors count as individuals
steps.stepSummary: The sailors are considered יחידים, not a צבור, so their case does not contradict רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: These people are also like individuals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the sailor challenge. Even a group of sailors is treated like individuals, so רבי יוחנן's rule about a צבור is untouched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same split as Step 15: a יחיד cannot tear up a decree after it is sealed, but a צבור can. A shipload of sailors, even if there are many of them, is not the whole community. So the rule for individuals applies to them.

keyTerms.meaning: they are like, they are considered

steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges fail. The rain case had another solution, and sailors count as יחידים. רבי יוחנן's rule stands: a צבור's תשובה can tear up a גזר דין, but a יחיד's cannot after the decree is sealed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It defines what counts as a צבור: a large group is not enough. It must be the community as a whole.

phrases.english: These too are like individuals.
phrases.notes: "Too" points back to Step 15, where the ברייתא was explained as talking about a יחיד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21 by using the יחיד versus צבור split from Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the group is classified as individuals.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought a group of sailors counts as a צבור, so their case would contradict רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sailors are considered יחידים, so the rule for individuals, that crying out after the decree is not answered, applies to them.

steps.title: בלוריא asks about two clashing פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: With תא שמע, the גמרא brings a story. בלוריא הגיורת asked רבן גמליאל how one פסוק can say ה׳ does not show favor while another says ה׳ will show favor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: בלוריא the convert asked רבן גמליאל: Your תורה says ה׳ 'does not show favor', and it also says 'ה׳ will show favor to you.' How can both be true?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new source with תא שמע. In the story, בלוריא asks about two פסוקים that seem to say opposite things about ה׳ showing favor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק says ה׳ 'does not lift faces', meaning He shows no favor. The ברכת כהנים says 'ה׳ will lift His face to you', meaning He will show favor. The answer to this clash will matter for our larger question of when ה׳ accepts תשובה and changes a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who converted to Judaism
Literally 'lifting the face': showing favor or going easy on someone

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאֲלָה בְּלוֹרְיָא הַגִּיּוֹרֶת אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: Beloreya the convert asked Rabban Gamliel:
It is written in your Torah: "who does not show favor"
and it is written: "ה׳ shall show favor to you"?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שָׁאֲלָה בְּלוֹרְיָא הַגִּיּוֹרֶת אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the sailors' case, the גמרא brings a new source that touches on when ה׳ accepts תשובה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How do 'He does not show favor' and 'ה׳ will show favor to you' fit together?

steps.title: רבי יוסי הכהן's parable of the king and the loan
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הכהן answers with a parable. A borrower swore by the king's life and did not repay. The king forgave the insult to himself but sent him to make peace with the lender. In the same way, ה׳ shows favor for sins against Him, but not for sins against other people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הכהן joined in and said to her: Let me give you a parable. A man lent his friend a מנה and set the due date in front of the king. The borrower swore by the king's life to repay, but the date came and he did not pay. He came to make peace with the king. The king said: I forgive the insult to me, but go make peace with your friend. Here too, one פסוק speaks about sins between a person and ה׳, and the other speaks about sins between a person and his fellow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הכהן resolves בלוריא's question with a parable. Each פסוק is talking about a different kind of sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king can forgive the insult to himself, but he cannot give up the friend's money. So 'ה׳ will show favor' applies to sins against ה׳, which He forgives. 'He does not show favor' applies to sins against other people, which ה׳ does not forgive until the victim is appeased.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable: a story used to explain an idea
A sum of money, one hundred coins
To appease, to make peace with someone
Between a person and another person

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יוסי הכהן's answer splits the פסוקים by type of sin and says nothing about decrees. The next line tells us that רבי עקיבא later gave a different answer to the same clash.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei the Kohen joined in with her.
He said to her: I will give you a parable.
To what is the matter similar?
To a person who lent his friend a maneh
phrases.notes: Literally 'who has a claim on his friend for a maneh.' He is the lender.

phrases.english: and set a due date for him in front of the king,
and the borrower swore to him by the life of the king.
The time came, and he did not repay him.
He came to make peace with the king,
and the king said to him: The insult to me is forgiven,
but go and make peace with your friend.
Here too:
here, it speaks about sins between a person and God;
phrases.notes: This is 'ה׳ will show favor to you.' ה׳ forgives these, like the king forgiving his own insult.

phrases.english: there, it speaks about sins between a person and his fellow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בלוריא's question from Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ shows favor for sins between a person and ה׳, but not for sins between people until the victim is appeased.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא comes with a different answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that רבי יוסי הכהן's answer stood until רבי עקיבא came and taught a different explanation. That teaching follows next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until רבי עקיבא came and taught:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next step. It tells us a new answer from רבי עקיבא is coming, and that it will take the place of רבי יוסי הכהן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'until רבי עקיבא came' show that the first answer was accepted only up to that point. רבי עקיבא's explanation, given in the next line, is the one that ties back to our question about decrees.

keyTerms.meaning: Until he came: this answer held until someone brought a new one

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not give רבי עקיבא's answer yet. It only announces it, and the answer itself comes in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.english: until Rabbi Akiva came and taught:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Signals that רבי יוסי הכהן's answer in Step 24 will be replaced by רבי עקיבא's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces רבי עקיבא's teaching on the two פסוקים, which comes next.
